text:
Priya (support): Customer reporting SSO break after cert rotation — users get 403 at our ACS. Customer says IdP shows successful assertion delivery. They included the SAML response and metadata link.
Thomas (eng-identity): Can you drop the IdP metadata URL + the exact ACS URL the customer is hitting? Also which binding (POST/Redirect) are they configured to use?
Priya (support): Metadata: https://idp.example-corp.com/metadata.xml
ACS observed: https://app.redwood.ai/_sso/acs (POST) — customer logs show HTTP 302 -> then 403 from our edge. SAML response snippet:
```
<samlp:Response ...>
  <saml:Assertion>
    <saml:Subject>
      <saml:NameID Format=...>eli@example.com</saml:NameID>
    </saml:Subject>
    <saml:Conditions/>
    <saml:AuthnStatement/>
  </saml:Assertion>
</samlp:Response>
```
Error in our logs: `RecipientMismatchError: assertion recipient https://app.redwood.ai/sso/acs != configured https://app.redwood.ai/_sso/acs`

Eli (customer): We didn't change the ACS recently. We saw the cert rotation notification from our IdP on Friday and immediately swapped to the new cert.
Carla (sre): Quick thought — our metadata fetching has a short TTL and an eventual-consistency path for cert rotation. If the IdP rotated and changed ordering of KeyDescriptor, older cached entry could still be used for a bit. Also trailing-slash differences often produce recipient mismatch.
Thomas (eng-identity): Looking at the IdP metadata, their AssertionConsumerService entries include two endpoints: one POST with index=1 at `/sso/acs` (no leading underscore) and one Redirect with index=0 at `/sso/acs/redirect`. Our SP config expects ACS URL `/_sso/acs` (note underscore). That mismatch will cause RecipientMismatchError even if signature validates against a rotated cert.
Priya (support): So the immediate repro is: IdP posts to `/sso/acs` -> our edge 302s to `/_sso/acs` -> SP rejects because assertion recipient doesn't exactly match post-target. Is that right?
Thomas (eng-identity): Yep. Two possible fixes: 1) Ask IdP to update their ACS entry to the exact URL we expect (including underscore and trailing slash), or 2) temporarily enable our tenant-level relaxed-recipient option which canonicalizes common redirects and accepts the 302 path. Option 2 is faster but less strict.
Carla (sre): Also need to invalidate our metadata cache after they re-push certs. The cache invalidation job is manual for this tenant and runs a refresh job — I can trigger it. If the cert order was changed, signature verification may pick the wrong cert until the updated metadata is fetched.
Priya (support): Customer willing to update metadata if that is the recommended stable fix. They asked if we can do anything on our side to avoid user downtime immediately.
Thomas (eng-identity): We can enable relaxed-recipient for the tenant for now (non-blocking change) and also trigger metadata refresh. But long-term we should ask them to publish the ACS URL exactly matching our SP. I'll enable the flag after approval.
SRE Oncall: I'm on it — creating a short-lived job to invalidate cache for tenant `example-corp` and forcing metadata re-fetch. Also posting incident ticket.
support-bot: Created ticket SR-123456 and escalated to eng-identity.

Priya (support): Before you flip the flag, can you confirm there are no security concerns with relaxing recipient checks for this tenant?
Thomas (eng-identity): It's a low-risk, short-lived workaround. It only relaxes exact recipient string comparison for common redirect shapes (leading underscore / trailing slash). We won't disable signature checks. I'll log the change and set an auto-revert in 72h.
Carla (sre): Cache invalidate started. Watching logs now. If the issue persists after metadata refresh, we should check KeyDescriptor ordering — some IdPs rotate by prepending the new key which changes which cert gets validated first. If their new cert isn't published with the expected KeyDescriptor use=signing, verification can fail intermittently.
Eli (customer): We pushed updated metadata a few minutes ago with POST to `/_sso/acs` and the new cert first. Please let us know when you see it.
Carla (sre): I see a metadata fetch 90s ago that contains the new cert order and the POST pointing to `/_sso/acs`. Triggered a full refresh across edges. Retrying login...
Carla (sre): Login successful from a customer test — assertion accepted. No 403s in the last 30s.
Priya (support): Confirmed with customer — they can sign in now. Thank you everyone.
Thomas (eng-identity): Follow-ups: 1) Add a KB entry about common recipient mismatch issues (underscore/trailing-slash + cert ordering). 2) Update our metadata fetcher to backoff-less aggressively when metadata changes during a rotation window. 3) Consider telemetry alert when RecipientMismatchError spikes during known cert rotation windows.
Priya (support): I'll file the KB and link SR-123456. Marking thread resolved unless anyone sees a reason to keep open. :white_check_mark:
summary: Customer SSO failing after IdP cert rotation and ACS endpoint mismatch. Triage identified recipient URL mismatch (underscore/trailing slash) plus metadata cache/KeyDescriptor ordering. Short-term relaxed-recipient flag + metadata invalidate fixed login; long-term doc + IdP metadata alignment recommended.
